narrative:
The assessment estimated an 84% probability that you would be a bad credit risk, meaning the lender judged repayment problems likely enough to deny the loan. This is not a certainty, but it is a high-risk score.

The leading reason was the status of your checking account: it is overdrawn (below 0 DM), a situation seen among only about 12.6% of approved applicants, and this was the strongest factor pushing toward a bad-credit decision. The second reason was the requested term of 60 months, far longer than the approved average of about 19 months, which increases uncertainty and pushed the decision further toward denial. Third, your property status is recorded as unknown or none; only about 7.8% of approved applicants share that profile, so the lack of property or collateral information also counted against you.

To improve your chances, ask the lender what conditions would make a revised application acceptable. Bring the checking account into good standing, request a smaller amount or shorter repayment period, and provide evidence of savings, a guarantor, or any property or collateral. Reapplying after these changes would give a clearer, stronger profile.
